title: The Hidden Hand of Economic Coercion
description: Threat of economic sanctions to coerce concessions; most successes occur at the threat stage.
evidence: Data show many successful coercion episodes end with sanctions threatened but not imposed.
p1_definition: A peer or the harmed party imposes, or credibly threatens, a cost on a deviator, usually at a cost to itself.
p2_definition: A central authority, often funded by members, applies fines or penalties for detected deviations under explicit rules, including standardized schedules and credible threats.

title: Conflict resolution in insect societies
description: Review of conflict resolution: policing, coercion, and kin structure regulating reproduction and caste.
p1_definition: The output of a deviation is reverted, removed, or rolled back so deviation yields nothing.
p2_definition: A peer or the harmed party imposes, or credibly threatens, a cost on a deviator, usually at a cost to itself.

title: The Economist as Engineer: Game Theory, Experimentation, and Computation as Tools for Design Economics
description: Stable (deferred-acceptance) clearinghouse design that removes incentives to contract early or strategically, sustaining participation in a centralized market.
evidence: Stable clearinghouses persist while unstable ones unravel; redesigned NRMP implemented.
p1_definition: Allocation and payment rules make truthful reporting or cooperation each agent's best strategy.
p2_definition: Tasks or resources are allocated through auctions, markets, or central matching rather than free negotiation, including rules for how agents discover and compare offers.

title: Promoting the use of end-to-end congestion control in the Internet
description: Proposes router mechanisms to identify and restrict the bandwidth of high-bandwidth best-effort flows that are unresponsive or not TCP-friendly, creating an incentive for end-to-end congestion control.
p1_definition: Access, privileges, or prices depend on an agent's reputation or proof of compliance.
p2_definition: A: Hard limits bound each agent's use of a shared resource or its rate of action. / B: A deviator is excluded, cut off, or quarantined (e.g., its links pruned by an overseer) for a bounded period or until a condition is met.

title: The Bitcoin Lightning Network: Scalable Off-Chain Instant Payments
description: Old channel states are invalidated by exchanging Breach Remedy Transactions; if a party broadcasts a revoked state, the counterparty can take all channel funds as a penalty.
p1_definition: An agent (or a third party on its behalf) posts collateral, or puts a future premium at risk, that is forfeited on breach or refunded on compliance.
p2_definition: Agents agree to enforceable conditional transfers or penalties, often executed automatically.

title: Sprite: a simple, cheat-proof, credit-based system for mobile ad-hoc networks
description: Nodes earn credit for forwarding others' messages (reported via receipts to a credit clearance service) and pay credit to send their own, making forwarding incentive-compatible without tamper-proof hardware.
evidence: Game-theoretic proof of cheat-proofness; simulation (not re-checked)
p1_definition: A central party pays for a cooperative act, verified behavior, contribution, or outcome.
p2_definition: Members pool resources, give without direct exchange, or trade services in mutual credit.

title: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
description: Analyzes AP2's signed Checkout and Payment Mandates, which protect transaction integrity after signing, and the unprotected pre-authorization A2A/MCP interactions.
evidence: descriptive threat analysis: 4 threat actors, 11 attack surfaces
p1_definition: Only pre-specified actions, scopes, zones, or time-bounded rights (leases) are permitted, including delegation specifications that bound a subagent's task.
p2_definition: Agents agree to enforceable conditional transfers or penalties, often executed automatically.

title: Reproducibility Study: Understanding Multi-Agent LLM Cooperation in the GovSim Framework
description: Independent GovSim reproduction that ablates the content of the universalization prompt.
evidence: Universalization improves performance, but the gain stems primarily from the numerical instructions in the prompt rather than the universalization principle itself.
p1_definition: Agents are told the consequences of their choices, the state of a shared resource or sustainable thresholds, or how their behavior compares with others'.
p2_definition: Agents' preferences or reasoning are shaped by training or prompting to value cooperative outcomes or to reason about others (e.g., universalization, perspective-taking).

title: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
description: Iterated Donor Game over generations of LLM agents who can observe recipients' recent behaviour; optional costly-punishment variant.
evidence: Cooperation evolution differs by base model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet > Gemini 1.5 Flash > GPT-4o); only Claude used costly punishment to raise scores; high seed sensitivity.
p1_definition: Agents help others according to the recipient's conduct toward third parties.
p2_definition: A: A designated or peer adjudicator issues a binding ruling, possibly after tiered escalation. / B: Behavior spreads by copying higher-payoff or expert others, or by selection among strategies.

title: Will Systems of LLM Agents Cooperate: An Investigation into a Social Dilemma
description: LLMs generate complete IPD strategies with aggressive/cooperative/neutral dispositions, which are then run in evolutionary population simulations.
evidence: Different LLMs bias the relative success of aggressive vs cooperative strategies (partial: agents are LLM-written programs, not LLMs acting per round).
p1_definition: An agent conditions its behavior toward a partner on that partner's past behavior toward it.
p2_definition: Behavior spreads by copying higher-payoff or expert others, or by selection among strategies.

title: Learning to Cooperate with Minimal Observability
description: Observer Model: RL agents learn from direct experience plus limited third-party observations; observability varied from none to one observer per game across population sizes; partner selection graphs analysed.
evidence: Direct experience alone fails in large societies; even minimal third-party observation yields robust cooperation.
p1_definition: Agents help others according to the recipient's conduct toward third parties.
p2_definition: Agents' actions are observed, inspected, audited, or disclosed (including inducement tests such as honeypots) so deviations can be detected.
